why: The span looks backwards: it runs until the previous strictly greater price. A stack of (price, span) pairs merges every smaller-or-equal day into today's entry, so each price is popped once. It teaches the span form of the monotonic stack, processed online.
hints: Today's span stops at which earlier day?
The nearest earlier day with a strictly higher price. Days with lower or equal prices are covered by today and can never stop a later span either.
Keep a stack of (price, span). For each price, start span = 1, pop while top price <= price and add its span, then push (price, span). Amortised O(1) per day.
pitfalls: The span counts today itself, so it is at least 1.
Pop on <= (equal prices are included in the span).
